answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network employs Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation. First, an agent must lock $15,000 in liquid collateral. Second, the hardware enclave generates a unique cryptographic identity through a secure TPM module. Third, the decentralized network validates this signature against the locked bond. An attacker attempting to spoof 100 identities must spend $1,500,000 and endure 72 hours of verification. This security wall is as deep as a canyon. Like a precious jade relic hidden within a complex karst landscape, each verified agent is unique and impossible to duplicate.
